status: offline iOS26 XNU provider-open semantics review

observations: kIOServiceSeize is documented as requesting withdrawal from the current owner.
open() locks the provider for arbitration and calls its virtual handleOpen().
Base IOService::handleOpen() accepts the first owner; kIOServiceSeize asks the existing owner to close before replacing it.

register_maps.observation: Retains the actual GPU/GMU providers and resource descriptors; acquireHostGpuRegisterWindow forwards those identities, the code descriptor, pre-SCACHE values and selected software profile to the supplied authority callback. It does not call IOService::open.

register_authority.observation: The callback contract requires a retained actual owner for the complete GPU/GMU/AO register configuration window and exclusion of GPU, CPU and firmware competitors.

board_owner.observation: ZornGen7DarwinBoardOwner inherits OSObject, so it is not itself an IOService client for open().

conclusion.next_action: Prepare a separate bounded CPU-only K80 iOS26 provider census under the fixed Recovery watchdog. Capture the actual GPU/GMU service metaclass, parent identity and open-state scalars without enabling GPU startup or touch. Implement a retained provider owner only after those identities and their open semantics are bound to real service/resource lifetimes.
